Atlanta's revival came against weakened defenses. Its short turnaround and Matthews/Smith exits temper the near-term flip; Jackson has not been ruled out.

Long-range games retain provisional judgments rather than treating current injuries, early records or one final as guaranteed future conditions. Weather, playoff qualifiers and Week 18 rest are not invented.

assessments.summary: Reassessed all 207 eligible unstarted matchups after Tampa Bay's 24-16 Dallas win. Flip Pittsburgh at Tampa Bay to Tampa Bay 23-20; retain Dallas at Green Bay but lower its projection to 24-20, and retain Cincinnati at Miami at a lower 21-17. Refresh three other pregame paragraphs for Daniels' expected return and obsolete Dallas/Tampa premises without changing their winners. Preserve every locked pick, original explanation and frozen projected score; append the sourced Dallas incorrect-final review.

1.availability: Matthews' groin and Smith's concussion remain unresolved; Penix has played, unlike a speculative return.
1.name: Atlanta Falcons
1.news: The matchup preview confirms Penix's efficiency and Atlanta's strong rush defense; Henry remains a serious test.
1.performance: Penix's actual return coincides with 80 points against Green Bay and New Orleans; those defenses temper the signal, but the opening 16 points no longer describe the current offense.

10.availability: Hooker's concussion and Tate/Helm practice limitations are current risks; an IR practice window does not mean activation.
10.name: Tennessee Titans
10.news: The Texans preview identifies two winless teams; there is no confirmed new offensive solution to promote Ward's current production.
10.performance: Tennessee is 0-4 with 55 points; keeping Baltimore within six suggests resistance but not a sustained scoring turnaround.

11.availability: Allen's groin is limited, Key is expected out three to four weeks and Pierce remains on IR; later dates need new checks.
11.name: Indianapolis Colts
11.news: The Pittsburgh preview confirms improving defense but warns about Jones' turnovers and a hostile venue.
11.performance: Indianapolis has recovered from two opening losses, with close Houston and 30-13 Washington wins; Washington's depletion and 257 total yards temper the London result.

12.availability: Thornton's ankle surgery has a lengthy estimate; Rice's possible post-bye return is not clearance.
12.name: Kansas City Chiefs
12.news: No verified new issue undermines the underlying Mahomes/Walker offensive case; short-rest and road games still deserve narrower margins.
12.performance: Kansas City's 118-77 start includes stronger opponents as well as Miami; four wins support Mahomes without implying invulnerability.

13.availability: Jeanty's foot/ankle and Nailor's concussion require review; Thornton's IR practice window is not confirmed activation.
13.name: Las Vegas Raiders
13.news: The dated New England preview identifies Cousins' fast start and opposing defensive injuries; continuity is evidence, not a guaranteed result.
13.performance: Las Vegas scored 115 against Miami, the Chargers, New Orleans and Kansas City; the first three opponents temper its 3-1 start.

14.availability: Donald, Watson and Parkinson are not assured; Landman and Lake missed practice. Nacua's productive return is observed, not guessed.
14.name: Los Angeles Rams
14.news: The Buffalo preview supports a passing mismatch against injured corners while recognizing Allen's exceptional dual-threat offense.
14.performance: The Rams' 415-172 yardage edge over Philadelphia matters, but depleted opponents and Stafford's six interceptions limit extrapolation.

15.availability: Willis remains the listed quarterback; Douglas, Joly and line/secondary issues need checks, and Grant's practice window is not activation.
15.name: Miami Dolphins
15.news: The Cincinnati preview credits improving defense but records Willis' one passing touchdown and two interceptions through four games.
15.performance: Miami's 46 points and 0-4 record understate some improving run defense; the 15-10 Minnesota loss was competitive against a strong opponent.

16.availability: Darrisaw's concussion, O'Neill's knee, Jefferson's ankle and Addison's hamstring are unresolved; Donovan Jackson is on IR.
16.name: Minnesota Vikings
16.news: The Saints preview points to a difficult defensive test for Shough; practice limitations do not prove multiweek absences.
16.performance: Minnesota is 4-0 with 86 points scored and 51 allowed; defense is more persuasive than projecting runaway offensive scoring.

17.availability: Gonzalez, Davis, Barmore and Stevenson have current practice concerns; Brown on IR is not cleared by walking without a limp.
17.name: New England Patriots
17.news: The Raiders preview warns about secondary depletion; the Buffalo win deserves weight without erasing earlier Seattle/Jacksonville struggles.
17.performance: The 29-26 Buffalo win improves a previously low-scoring start; 65 points in four games still discourage treating it as an offensive breakout.

18.availability: Kamara's back and Olave's foot are limited; no current designation is assumed to persist to December.
18.name: New Orleans Saints
18.news: The Staley/Aikman dispute is commentary, not a personnel fix; Shough's competitive passing does not erase recent rushing concessions.
18.performance: New Orleans scored 105 but allowed 128; consecutive losses allowing 35 and 45 materially weaken an assumed home defensive edge.

19.availability: Thomas, Nabers, Skattebo and Likely are limited; Golston may have a lengthy neck absence, not a confirmed season-ending diagnosis.
19.name: New York Giants
19.news: The Washington preview confirms Winston is starting and Daniels is expected back; the identity-verified fixtures, not contradictory prose, control venue.
19.performance: The Giants' 36-24 Arizona win and 3-1 record improve their case, but Winston's interceptions and a 28-6 Rams loss preserve uncertainty.

2.availability: Moore's shoulder, Oliver's knee and several cornerback injuries threaten near-term execution; no long-term absence is assumed.
2.name: Buffalo Bills
2.news: The Rams preview identifies Buffalo's depleted coverage and red-zone defense, not a diminished Allen ceiling.
2.performance: Three opening wins precede a 29-26 New England loss; Allen remains productive, but 107 conceded points make defensive confidence inappropriate.

20.availability: Hall and Mitchell are doubtful, Parham remains week-to-week, and Patrick's return window does not guarantee availability.
20.name: New York Jets
20.news: The Cleveland preview supports a pressure/turnover concern; no verified new offensive acquisition justifies a near-term reset.
20.performance: The Jets' 76-84 totals include close Green Bay/Detroit losses and a 23-12 Chicago defeat; a Tennessee win alone does not establish attacking consistency.

21.availability: Barkley and Smith missed Thursday practice, Goedert is limited, and multiple defensive issues remain unresolved.
21.name: Philadelphia Eagles
21.news: The London preview describes an undermanned team; a center-trade claim is not treated as confirmed without a directly verified transaction.
21.performance: Philadelphia's 75-93 totals and 172 yards against the Rams weaken a depth-only forecast; early close wins were not dominant.

22.availability: Paris Johnson and Hunter Long are on IR, Adams is ruled out Sunday, and Love remains limited.
22.name: Arizona Cardinals
22.news: Harrison trade rumors are not a completed transaction; the current roster, rather than a rumored destination, controls this assessment.
22.performance: Arizona's 87-117 totals include competitiveness at San Francisco but a 36-24 Giants loss; the passing ceiling coexists with defensive leakage.

23.availability: Pittman is expected out multiple weeks, Harmon is on IR, Dean has a multiweek ankle concern and Dowdle is limited.
23.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
23.news: The Indianapolis preview documents tackling problems and a run-defense test without Harmon; McCarthy's commitment is not an already-delivered improvement.
23.performance: Pittsburgh is 2-2 with both wins at home and only 27 combined points in its road defeats; close Cincinnati/Cleveland games show substantial variance.

24.availability: Slater is expected out four to six weeks; Alt, Penning and Awosika missed practice, and McConkey/Johnston have current concerns.
24.name: Los Angeles Chargers
24.news: McDaniel's response to firing calls is not a coaching change; protection injuries remain more actionable than commentary.
24.performance: Four losses and 67 points include a more competitive Seattle performance; Herbert's talent is insufficient evidence of a completed turnaround.

25.availability: Evans' ribs, doubtful Bosa and Juszczyk's multiweek knee absence are relevant; Kirk's possible practice window does not establish return.
25.name: San Francisco 49ers
25.news: The Seattle preview frames a divisional road test; the 4-0 record does not eliminate coverage and pressure risks.
25.performance: San Francisco's 122-64 start includes a decisive Rams win and 24-14 Denver win, though Arizona scored 30 against it.

26.availability: Williams' ankle and secondary questions remain; Charbonnet will not be activated for the San Francisco game.
26.name: Seattle Seahawks
26.news: The San Francisco preview supports rivalry/venue importance without turning past playoff outcomes into present certainty.
26.performance: Seattle's 105-73 start has stronger scoring after the opener but a Washington loss; its Chargers win is not proof against elite offenses.

27.availability: Mayfield's thumb is expected to cost at least one more game; Daniels' improvement is observed. Thursday inactives are not presumed out indefinitely.
27.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
27.news: The verified recap confirms Irving's 165 rushing yards and two touchdowns and Daniels' 19-of-25 passing; this is a better current offense than the winless label implied.
27.performance: Tampa's 24-16 road win breaks the 0-4 start; 241 rushing yards and a turnover-free Daniels start are meaningful, but Dallas' defense limits generalization.

28.availability: Daniels is expected back with no stated limitations, not guaranteed game-day effectiveness; McLaurin and Diggs missed practice and Cosmi is uncertain.
28.name: Washington Commanders
28.news: The dated preview confirms the return plan and receiver depletion; stronger quarterback availability narrows rather than automatically reverses the Giants lean.
28.performance: Washington's 88-122 start includes a Seattle win but London execution/turnover problems; quarterback restoration may help without repairing every unit.

29.availability: Ekwonu is still some way from returning, Legette is on IR and Jackson's surgery has an eight-week estimate; Coker/Phillips/Freeling returns remain possibilities.
29.name: Carolina Panthers
29.news: A bye creates recovery opportunity, not confirmed clearance; no new verified report resolves protection and coverage concerns.
29.performance: Carolina's 121 points show scoring upside, but the Chicago 59-point concession and 109 total allowed limit a balanced-team claim.

3.availability: Williams remains out with a hamstring injury, Bagent is expected Sunday, Swift is limited and Monangai's toe/thumb is uncertain.
3.name: Chicago Bears
3.news: The Green Bay preview confirms a productive running scheme but also significant current running-back uncertainty.
3.performance: The 59-point Carolina opener inflates 112 total points; subsequent defense against Minnesota, Philadelphia and the Jets is more repeatable support.

30.availability: Current secondary and offensive-line questions need near-kickoff checks; depth-chart order does not establish a healthy lineup.
30.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
30.news: The London preview supports recent continuity and Philadelphia depletion; remaining overseas travel and later availability still matter.
30.performance: Jacksonville's 104-53 start includes decisive Cleveland/New England wins and a five-point Cincinnati win; a seven-point Denver loss keeps it fallible.

33.availability: Jackson's ankle remains questionable, Flowers is limited and Humphrey missed practice; an unverified Jurgens trade is not assumed complete.
33.name: Baltimore Ravens
33.news: The Atlanta preview confirms Huntley as the contingency, not the announced starter, and Henry's importance against a strong rush defense.
33.performance: Baltimore scored 116 and conceded 96; Indianapolis/Dallas wins show upside, but a Saints loss and six-point Tennessee win discourage dominance claims.

34.availability: Dell and linemen on IR have practice-window activity, not confirmed activation; Al-Shaair and other current designations remain uncertain.
34.name: Houston Texans
34.news: The Tennessee preview offers a weak-scoring opponent but no verified personnel cure; Stroud's upside remains a provisional matchup edge.
34.performance: Houston is 0-4 despite competitive Buffalo, Indianapolis and Dallas losses; 84-109 totals support a possible narrow rebound, not a dominant projection.

4.availability: Chase's concussion clearance and Higgins' groin remain uncertain; defensive line and safety practice limitations also matter.
4.name: Cincinnati Bengals
4.news: The Miami preview supports Cincinnati's pressure advantage, while warning that neither top receiver is assured to play.
4.performance: Wins over Tampa Bay and Houston preceded losses to Pittsburgh and Jacksonville; Burrow's 72.2% completions against Jacksonville support competence despite a two-game skid.

5.availability: Interior defenders Hall and Graham and guard Jenkins have current availability concerns; injury-feed silence elsewhere is not clearance.
5.name: Cleveland Browns
5.news: The dated Jets preview notes Watson's clutch contributions; no new confirmed roster change displaces the modest defensive case.
5.performance: Three close wins followed the 34-10 Jacksonville loss; a negative differential prevents treating the 3-1 record as dominant form.

6.availability: Lamb's quadriceps and Guyton's back need new checks before Green Bay; good X-rays do not prove clearance. Porter missed Tampa with illness.
6.name: Dallas Cowboys
6.news: The verified final shows three turnovers, only 50 rushing yards and 241 rushing yards allowed; added defensive personnel did not guarantee a repair.
6.performance: Dallas has scored 138 and allowed 136 through five games; the 24-16 Tampa loss exposes turnover and rush-defense volatility after three 31-point games.

7.availability: Surtain's ankle, Moss' ribs and Bryant's availability are current concerns, not automatic future-week absences.
7.name: Denver Broncos
7.news: Dated reports say Payton will take over playcalling; a change of caller is not evidence of an already-improved offense.
7.performance: Home wins over Jacksonville and the Rams followed the Kansas City defeat, then a 24-14 loss at San Francisco; 74 points in four games limit the offensive ceiling.

8.availability: Current practice designations require review near kickoff; no depth-chart listing establishes full availability.
8.name: Detroit Lions
8.news: No verified new coaching or completed trade report warrants replacing the scoring-based matchup case.
8.performance: Detroit's 119 points show offensive capacity, but 127 conceded points and the earlier 95 in three games weaken a defense-based case.

9.availability: Parsons remains out; the preview confirms season-ending Cooper, Bako-Bewele and Reed injuries and Jacobs' commissioner-exempt status.
9.name: Green Bay Packers
9.news: The rivalry preview documents structural absences and weak rush defense; current reserve-feed omissions cannot be treated as an all-clear.
9.performance: The 17-14 Tampa win is useful but narrow; losses to Minnesota and Atlanta and only 73 total points still expose protection and rushing problems.

explanationRevisions.paragraph: I expect the Indianapolis Colts to beat the Washington Commanders because its improving defense should make Washington work harder for scoring opportunities. With the game listed at a neutral venue in London, this case will rely on the matchup rather than a usual home-crowd advantage.

I expect the Baltimore Ravens to beat the Tennessee Titans because Baltimore's offense should create more scoring opportunities than Tennessee could answer. The home setting should help, but neither that setting nor the expected advantage will make the result certain.

I expect the Buffalo Bills to beat the New England Patriots because Josh Allen was seen as the decisive quarterback advantage and a way to keep Buffalo's offense moving. The home setting should help, but neither that setting nor the expected advantage will make the result certain.

I expect the Chicago Bears to beat the New York Jets because Chicago's improving defense should disrupt the Jets and control the pace of the game. The home setting should help, but neither that setting nor the expected advantage will make the result certain.

I expect the Jacksonville Jaguars to beat the Cincinnati Bengals because Jacksonville's defensive approach should remain effective away from home. That advantage will still need to hold up on the road, and the opponent could win if the expected matchup edge does not materialize.

I expect the Dallas Cowboys to beat the Houston Texans because Dallas should generate more reliable offense than Houston in this matchup. That advantage will still need to hold up on the road, and the opponent could win if the expected matchup edge does not materialize.

I expect the Arizona Cardinals to edge the New York Giants. Dart's reported season-ending injury leaves New York relying on replacement quarterbacks, and the recorded concern about Andrew Thomas adds protection uncertainty. Arizona's recent offensive resistance against San Francisco should give it a chance to exploit that disruption, but the long trip east and the Giants' home defense could keep the matchup close.

I picked Pittsburgh expecting Rodgers to provide the quarterback edge, but that choice was wrong in Cleveland's 27-24 win. Pittsburgh threw two interceptions, allowed five sacks, and converted only four of 13 third downs, while Cleveland went four for 10 and made the decisive 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left. The pregame case put too much weight on the expected quarterback advantage and too little on protection, drive efficiency, and Cleveland's ability to finish the game; the Steelers pick remains recorded as incorrect.

explanationRevisions.paragraph: The Cardinals pick put too much weight on New York's quarterback disruption and Arizona's previous competitive showing against San Francisco. Jameis Winston instead threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns, while Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions and Arizona managed 270 total yards. The Giants erased an early 14-3 deficit, and Deonte Banks' 98-yard interception return on the final play sealed the 36-24 result. Arizona's expected offensive edge failed to materialize, and New York's replacement quarterback and late defensive stops were more effective than the forecast allowed.

sources.title: Winston throws 3 TD passes and Banks' pick-6 seals Giants' 36-24 win over Cardinals

explanationRevisions.paragraph: The Eagles pick overestimated what home field could do for a depleted offense. Philadelphia led 20-10 at halftime but finished with only 172 total yards, went 0-for-12 on third down and scored nothing after halftime. A failed fourth-down attempt gave the Rams a chance to stay in it, and Kyren Williams scored two rushing touchdowns in the final four minutes to complete Los Angeles' 24-20 comeback. The expected rebound never became sustained offensive control, so the home-field rationale did not survive the second half.

sources.title: Rams rally behind Stafford, Williams from 10 points down in 4th quarter to beat Eagles 24-20

explanationRevisions.paragraph: The Bills pick leaned too heavily on Josh Allen as the decisive quarterback advantage. Drake Maye answered with 269 passing yards and three touchdowns, while New England gained 405 yards and scored touchdowns on all three red-zone trips. Buffalo led 26-21 after Keon Coleman's touchdown, but Maye connected with Efton Chism III for the go-ahead score with 1:50 left, and Craig Woodson intercepted Allen on the following possession. Both teams committed two turnovers; New England's sustained offense and late execution, rather than the expected Buffalo control, decided the 29-26 game.

sources.title: Maye overcomes his two turnovers with 3 TD passes in Patriots' 29-26 win over Bills

explanationRevisions.paragraph: I picked Detroit because I expected Jahmyr Gibbs to give the Lions a rushing edge, but Carolina won 32-26 at home and reversed that matchup. Gibbs was held to 46 rushing yards on 15 carries, while Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Bryce Young completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards, including two touchdowns to Tetairoa McMillan, who caught 14 passes for 192 yards. Carolina scored on six straight possessions after punting on its opening drive, and Detroit's offense often stalled near scoring range, settling for four Jake Bates field goals despite Jared Goff's 412 passing yards.

explanationRevisions.paragraph: My Dallas pick was wrong because the expected scoring reliability and home-field edge did not survive three turnovers and a defense that allowed Tampa Bay 241 rushing yards. Irving ran for 165 yards and scored twice, while rookie Jalon Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes without an interception; Tampa's 17-point third quarter turned Dallas' 10-7 halftime lead into a 24-10 deficit. Prescott's two interceptions and Turpin's lost kickoff fumble helped create that swing, and Dallas managed only 50 rushing yards despite Prescott's 316 passing yards. Lamb's quadriceps exit added an offensive limitation, but the verified turnovers and rushing imbalance, rather than home field or the earlier scoring streak, explain why Tampa won 24-16.
